newsitem.title: USA: Clinton urged to fix NAFTA during Mexico trip.
newsitem.headline: Clinton urged to fix NAFTA during Mexico trip.

text.p: Labor and environmental groups on Monday called the North American Free Trade Agreement a failure and urged President Clinton to try to fix it during his visit to Mexico this week.
"NAFTA is a failure. It must be fixed," Friends of the Earth President Brent Blackwelder said at a news conference.

Richard Trumka, Secretary-Treasurer of the AFL-CIO labor organization, said 420,000 U.S. jobs had been lost since the free trade agreement between the United States, Mexico and Canada was approved in 1993 and the U.S. trade deficit with both nations had increased from $9 billion to $39 billion.

"When President Clinton travels to Mexico today, we urge him to use this trip to look beneath the surface and assess first hand how NAFTA has failed to live up to its promises on both sides of the border," Trumka said.

Clinton is scheduled to spend three days in Mexico on a trip that also includes stops in Costa Rica and Barbados. He made passage of NAFTA one of his first major priorities when he became president in 1993.
Trumka said that although Mexico has gained jobs, the average hourly pay of Mexican workers had declined 36 percent.
Blackwelder and Sierra Club Chairman Michael McCloskey said pollution along the U.S.-Mexico border had increased since NAFTA was approved because of the industrial growth in the area.
The Teamsters Union warned that thousands of unsafe Mexico trucks were being allowed into the United States every day because of NAFTA and urged that those provisions of the treaty be renegotiated.
The groups opposed approval of NAFTA and said they would fight its expansion to nations in Central and South America unless the current treaty was improved.
